newsitem.title: USA: US energy prices fall on ACCESS despite API draws.
newsitem.headline: US energy prices fall on ACCESS despite API draws.

text.p: U.S. energy futures prices fell in early ACCESS trade despite reports of lower inventories, traders said.
The trade group American Petroleum Institute showed crude stocks nationwide decreased by 5.7 million barrels to 313 million.
"Surprisingly, we've seen a bit of a sell-off in crude tonight," one trader said.
October NYMEX crude traded $23.07 a barrel, off 17 cents from the settle. A heavy volume of 1,500 lots changed hands.
Traders said many players felt crude was overvalued following the U.S. bombing of Iraq and suspension of the country's 700,000 barrels per day export agreement with the United Nations.
Iraq's contribution to world production was already discounted by the market, traders said, even before the conflict began this week.
October gasoline lost 0.11 cent to reach 62.85 cents a gallon on ACCESS on a moderate 100 lots traded.
October heating oil dropped 0.31 cent a gallon to trade at 63.90 cents on 500 lots traded.
